summary: Thomas Watters (1840–1901) was a scholar in sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his B.A. from Queen's University Belfast (1857–1861) and Queen's University of Ireland (circa 1857–1861).
Thomas Zehnder (born 1965) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He earned his PhD at the University of Zurich, studying under supervisor Alexander Lubotsky.

Thubten Chodron (born 1950) works in Buddhist studies. Educated at UCLA, USC, Kopan Monastery, and Dorje Pamo Monastery, she held posts at Istituto Lama Tzong Khapa, Amitabha Buddhist Centre, and Dharma Friendship Foundation before founding and serving as abbess of Sravasti Abbey.

Thubten Jigme Norbu (1922–2008) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studying under Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley and Ngawang Nyima. He served as a professor at Indiana University (1965–1992) and as director of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives.
Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley studied under the 13th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche. He taught Dagpo Rinpoche, Tenzin Gyatso, Thubten Jigme Norbu, and Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.

Thubten Zopa Rinpoche (1946–2023) was a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology figure who studied at Dungkar Monastery and under Yeshe Thubten, among others. He co-founded Kopan Monastery, Tushita Meditation Centre, and FPMT, where he served as spiritual director from 1984.

Thupten Jinpa (born 1958) works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Educated at Zongkar Choede, Ganden Monastery, and Cambridge, he was a fellow at Girton College (1996–1999), founded the Institute of Tibetan Classics, and held a research post at Stanford.

Thupten Samphel (1956–2022) was a Tibetologist who studied at St. Stephen's College, the University of Delhi, and Columbia University (~1982–1983). He held a post at the Tibet Policy Institute from 2012 to 2018.
Thushini S. Jayawardena works in religious studies. She studied under traditional teacher Satya Narayan Goenka and earned a PhD from Auckland University of Technology by 2017.

Théodore Pavie (1811–1896) was an Indologist and sinologist who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at the Collège de France (1852–1857) and taught Hebrew lessons and lectures at the Catholic University of the West in 1862.

Tianshu Zhu works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After earning an MA at Northwest University and a PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington, Zhu held positions at Shaanxi History Museum, Northwest University, Korea University, and Ohio State.

Tilak Kariyawasam (born 1942) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as head of the Department of Pali and Buddhist Studies at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1993) and Dean of the Graduate School at International Buddhist College (attested 2014).

Tilmann Vetter (1937–2012) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Vienna under Erich Frauwallner in 1962 and became a professor at Leiden University in 1974.

Timothy Hugh Barrett (born 1947) is a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at the University of Cambridge and Yale University, he taught at Cambridge (attested 1981) and became a professor at SOAS University of London in 1986.

Timothy Lenz works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Washington under Richard Salomon and Collett Cox, and later held posts there, including as professor (attested 2017).

Timothy Lubin works in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Columbia University in 1994, held a post at Washington and Lee University (attested 2012–2020), and collaborated on the DHARMA project.
Tina Rasmussen works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied under traditional teacher Pa-Auk Sayadaw and completed an MA supervised by Christian K. Wedemeyer.

Tirumalai Krishnamacharya (1888–1989) worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Queen's College, Benares, and the University of Mysore, and under Ramamohana Brahmachari, later teaching at Maharaja's Sanskrit College, Mysore (1931) and Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College.

Tissa Rajapatirana (born 1933) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD under Jan Willem de Jong at the Australian National University (1966–1974), where he later held a post attested in 1988.
Tiziana Pontillo (born 1969) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She studied at the University of Cagliari in 2016 and held a post there in 2022.
